content.text:
A long long time ago, there was a cowherd family in Tarakeshwar.
Every day Deba and Deep took the cows out for grazing.
They used to return in the late evening together with all the cows.
One day, Deba asked, "How do we know that we have not lost any cows?"
They did not know how to count.
What could Deba and Deep do?

tool_config.screen: Same frame as every tool (step dots, Hint, Reset, Back, Next; no score, no timer). The picture is the stone slab from the story, its marks standing in groups of five, with the shed gate beside it. PHASE 1, get ready: a small slab labelled Practice (the plan's own) holds 13 marks: two groups of five and one group of three. One line: 'The herd is big. Marks stand in groups of five.' PHASE 2, play: the child taps each group and a running total shows 5, 10, 13. Then ten cows walk in with the line 'Ten cows come home. Strike out their marks.' and the child taps a group of five twice to strike out ten marks. Three marks stay standing, and the line 'Which marks are the cows still out?' asks the child to tap them. PHASE 3, the book's questions on the real slab, one after another. (1) Count the marks: nine groups of five and one group of two. Each tap shows only that group's own count and no running total; the child adds them and types the number of cows on the number pad (digits 0 to 9 and an OK tile), to fill the blank 'they had ___ cows'. (2) The next day the cows walk in, and each time five cows enter the child taps a group of five to strike it out, nine times. The last group of two stays standing and the gate stays empty. Then three answer cards show for why Deba and Deep were worried: 'Two marks were still left, but no cows were outside.' and two wrong cards, 'Every mark was struck out and every cow was home.' and 'The wall had too many marks to count.' The child taps one card. Last, the child types on the number pad how many cows had reached home. (3) Hemant's herd: a cow row and a sheep row, each headed by a picture of a cow or a real sheep, with '36 cows' and '23 sheep' in words. Each row has its own Make 1 mark and Make 5 marks buttons, so the row is chosen by the button the child taps. The child makes marks for his cows and his sheep, kept in separate rows. A tap on a mark takes it back.

tool_config.screen: Same frame as every tool (step dots, Hint, Reset, Back, Next; no score, no timer). Name cards lie flat on a table (the name_tag card, string tucked under; no hooks, no row on a wall). No card has a ring at the start. A ring appears only when the child taps a letter, and its meaning shows beside it: an orange ring for a starting letter with the words 'starting letter', a blue ring for an ending letter with the words 'ending letter'. No middle letter is ever ringed. PHASE 1, get ready: one card, Mala, lies alone on the table, no ring, with one line, 'A name has a first letter and a last letter. Find them.' PHASE 2, play: three practice cards, Kartik, Mahesh and Deba, come one at a time with the line 'Tap the first letter. Then tap the last letter.' The child taps the first letter and an orange ring appears with the words 'starting letter'. The child taps the last letter and a blue ring appears with the words 'ending letter'. A tap on a middle letter gives a gentle shake. PHASE 3, the book's questions, one after another, with the eight friends of the book (Deba, Deep, Hemant, Mahesh, Kartik, Teji, Jojo, Mala) as name cards on the table, labelled Practice with the book's friends. Each card now shows its orange ring and its blue ring, and a row of number tiles from 1 to 8 sits under the table. (1) 'My name' is Mala (the child may tap another card); the child taps the card, then taps its starting letter. (2) With the switch on Starting letter, the child drags cards into piles: a card goes onto a pile with the same orange-ring letter or starts a new pile. The child counts the pile of their own letter and taps the number tile with that count. (3) The child taps the tallest pile or piles, a tie is allowed, and taps the number tile for the count in it. (4) The switch is turned to Ending letter and the cards are sorted by their blue-ring letter; the child counts the names that end like their own and taps the number tile with that count. (5) An alphabet strip from A to Z: the child taps every letter that starts no name, and a tap on a starting letter gives a gentle shake.

tool_config.title: Group the Cards Two Ways
tool_config.learning_objective: Students put things into two groups by a rule, say what is common in a group, and regroup them another way.
tool_config.screen: Same frame as every tool (step dots, Hint, Reset, Back, Next; no score, no timer). Large cards and two big dotted boxes. Two rounds, one for each set of cards. PHASE 1, get ready: Teji stands beside a heap of ten picture cards with no names on them, and her two boxes, labelled 'Those that eat food' and 'Those that don't eat food', the words of the story. PHASE 2, play, round 1: with the line 'Put each card in Teji's group.' the child drags each of the ten picture cards into the box of Teji's rule where it fits. A card in the wrong box slides back with a reason, and a card in the right box settles in. When all ten are placed, the same cards move into two other boxes with no labels: Jojo's groups. PHASE 3, the book's questions, one after another. (1) Jojo's groups: for each group the child taps what is common from four rule cards (Things that fly, Things that do not fly, Things that eat food, Things with wings). Round 2: (2) the eight household cards (TV, Chair, Lamp, Bed, Clock, Fan, Pillow, Blanket) go into two note-pad panels labelled 'Things that need electricity' and 'Things that don't need electricity'. (3) The same eight cards go into two panels with no labels, grouped another way. Then four rule cards show (Things we use for sleeping, Things that need electricity, Things that fly, Things that eat food) and the child taps the rule card that tells why the two groups differ. Check my groups passes only when every card is in one group, the groups are not the electricity groups, and the tapped rule card fits the two groups (the plan's rule: Bed, Pillow and Blanket against the other five).

visual_key.teji: a girl with black hair in two plaits tied with red bows, in a red dress with white dots
visual_key.jojo: a boy with black curly hair in a yellow T-shirt with a blue-green band across the middle

visual_key.group_box: a rounded box with a dotted outline that holds the cards of one group; a writing group is a note-pad panel with spiral rings down its left edge and a coloured tab on top: lilac with the labels Things that need electricity and Things that don't need electricity, or pale green with blue tabs and no labels

visual_key.tick_and_cross: a round green badge with a white tick, and a round green badge with a white cross
visual_key.place_sign: a yellow signboard with black letters in more than one script and in English capitals: VENKATANARASIMHARAJUVARIPETA, IB and OD
visual_key.mala: a schoolgirl with brown hair in two ponytails, in a blue pinafore with a yellow satchel on her way to school

visual_key.hair_style_pictures: six head-and-shoulder pictures in pale green table cells: one high ponytail; two long plaits with blue ribbons; short curly hair; wavy hair with a blue hair clip; short straight black hair; two low ponytails
